bio: Most people only sell a home a few times in their lives. It is one of the biggest financial decisions they will ever make and Kirby Chan has built his career around helping it go right.

Kirby is a Broker and the co-founder of Kirby Chan & Co. Real Estate Team, working across Toronto, Markham, Richmond Hill and the Greater Toronto Area. The team started with a simple commitment to honest, client-first real estate.

His approach is straightforward. He does not push. He listens, he advises and he helps you make the decision that is right for you, not the one that is convenient for him. That is why referrals and returning clients are the foundation of the business.

Kirby runs the team with co-founder Carrie Szeto and a group of dedicated specialists. Together they bring local market knowledge, modern digital marketing and a real understanding of what homeowners across the Greater Toronto Area need when it is time to move.
about.quote: He does not push. He listens, he advises and he helps you make the decision that is right for you.

philosophy.title: Honest advice first
philosophy.body: We tell you what you need to hear, not what you want to hear. Sometimes the honest answer is to wait.

philosophy.title: Local knowledge
philosophy.body: Toronto, Markham and Richmond Hill are our markets. We follow the sales street by street and know how prices differ from one neighbourhood to the next.

philosophy.title: Clients for life
philosophy.body: Most of our business comes from past clients and their referrals. That is the result of doing right by people.

services.lede: Every move is different. These are the situations we help with most often, with a plain description of how we handle each one.

buying.name: Buying a Home
buying.summary: A clear search, careful checks and offers based on real comparable sales.
buying.body: We help you set a realistic budget, narrow the neighbourhoods that fit your life and check each property carefully before you make an offer.

selling.name: Selling a Home
selling.summary: A price we can defend, proper preparation and marketing that reaches buyers.
selling.body: We price your home on real comparable sales, tell you which preparation is worth the money and market the property to the buyers most likely to pay for it.

luxury.name: Luxury Homes
luxury.summary: Thin comparables, a small buyer pool and no room for a pricing mistake.
luxury.body: Toronto luxury homes have few direct comparables and, since April 1, 2026, higher municipal land transfer tax over $3 million. We price with care, present the home properly and protect your privacy.

relocation.name: Relocation
relocation.summary: Choosing a neighbourhood you have never lived in, usually on a deadline.
relocation.body: Moving to Toronto from another city or country? We explain the neighbourhoods, transit and costs honestly so you can choose with confidence, often from a distance.

downsizing.name: Downsizing
downsizing.summary: Decades in one house and a move that has to happen in the right order.
downsizing.body: We plan the sale and the next home together at a pace that suits you. We also help with the practical side of leaving a long-time family home.

upsizing.name: Upsizing
upsizing.summary: Two transactions, one timeline and a gap that has to be financed.
upsizing.body: Selling one home and buying a larger one means two deals that have to line up. We plan the order, the timing and the financing questions before you commit.

first-time-buyers.name: First-Time Buyers
first-time-buyers.summary: A real budget, a realistic neighbourhood list and no surprises at closing.
first-time-buyers.body: We walk you through every step, from mortgage pre-approval to closing costs, so you always know what comes next and what it will cost.

new-construction.name: New Construction
new-construction.summary: A builder contract written by the builder and a closing that is years away.
new-construction.body: Pre-construction and new homes come with contracts that favour the builder. We review the details with you and explain the risks before you sign.

investors.name: Investors
investors.summary: Numbers that have to work before the story does.
investors.body: We look at rent, carrying costs, City rules and resale before the pitch, so an investment property in Toronto makes sense on paper first.

estate-sales.name: Estate Sales
estate-sales.summary: A sale run by an executor, usually during a very hard year.
estate-sales.body: We help executors and families sell an estate property with patience and clear communication, working alongside the estate lawyer at every step.

separation-and-divorce.name: Separation and Divorce
separation-and-divorce.summary: A shared home, two people moving on and a sale that has to be fair to both.
separation-and-divorce.body: We keep both parties equally informed, work alongside each person's lawyer and run a sale that is transparent from pricing to closing.

neighbourhoods.lede: Each Toronto neighbourhood has its own housing, transit and price level. Here is a short introduction to each one.

leaside.tagline: Detached and semi-detached streets beside the Line 5 Eglinton stations.
leaside.body: More than half the homes in Leaside are single-detached houses (2021 Census). Leaside station on Line 5 Eglinton is at Bayview Avenue, with Laird and Sunnybrook Park stations further east along Eglinton.

lawrence-park.tagline: Detached houses, ravine parks and Line 1 at Lawrence.
lawrence-park.body: A neighbourhood of detached homes around the Lawrence Park Ravine and Blythwood Ravine Park, with Lawrence station on Line 1 and Eglinton station at its southern edge.

yonge-eglinton.tagline: Condo towers where Line 1 meets Line 5.
yonge-eglinton.body: Eglinton station is the interchange between Line 1 Yonge University and Line 5 Eglinton. Most homes in the area are in apartment buildings of five storeys or more, with older detached and semi-detached streets on either side.

don-mills.tagline: A planned community near the Line 5 Eglinton stations.
don-mills.body: Banbury-Don Mills mixes detached houses with condo apartments. Wynford, Aga Khan Park & Museum and Don Valley stations on Line 5 Eglinton are near its southern edge.

the-annex.tagline: Victorian houses and apartments on Line 1 and Line 2.
the-annex.body: The Annex sits on Bloor Street with Spadina, St George and Bathurst stations. It includes the East Annex heritage conservation district and most of its homes are apartments or converted houses.

bayview-village.tagline: Condos on the Sheppard subway, detached streets behind them.
bayview-village.body: Bayview, Bessarion and Leslie stations on Line 4 Sheppard serve the area, with a City community centre and library at Bayview and Sheppard. Most sales are condo apartments.

willowdale.tagline: North York Centre condos along the Yonge subway.
willowdale.body: Finch, North York Centre and Sheppard-Yonge stations run through Willowdale on Line 1. Most homes near Yonge Street are in apartment buildings of five storeys or more, with detached houses on the streets to the west (2021 Census).

downtown-waterfront.tagline: Condo apartments between Union Station and the lake.
downtown-waterfront.body: Almost every home here is in an apartment building of five storeys or more (2021 Census). Union Station, with Line 1 and GO trains, is at its northern edge.

high-park.body: High Park, Keele and Runnymede stations on Line 2 serve streets of detached and semi-detached houses and apartment buildings around High Park.

the-beaches.tagline: Lakeside streets and the Kingswood Road South heritage district.
the-beaches.body: Detached and semi-detached houses make up most sales in The Beaches, near the lake, with Main Street and Woodbine stations on Line 2 to the north.

riverdale.tagline: Semi-detached streets on the east side of the Don.
riverdale.body: Semi-detached and row houses make up a large share of sales in North and South Riverdale, with four Line 2 stations from Broadview to Donlands and the Riverdale heritage conservation district.

islington-village.tagline: Houses near Islington station and condos at Kipling.
islington-village.body: The TRREB community covers detached streets around Islington and the Etobicoke City Centre condo buildings near Kipling station, where Line 2 connects with Kipling GO.
